detailed_rationale:
Firstsource Solutions (RP-Sanjiv Goenka group) is a business-process-management (BPM/BPO) provider across Healthcare, Banking & Financial Services, and Communications-Media-Technology verticals, with delivery centers across India, the US, UK and Philippines. FY26 was a genuine milestone year: revenue crossed the $1 billion mark for the first time, up 19.7% YoY, with normalized PAT up 26.9%. Q4 FY26 alone delivered net profit of Rs 205.24 crore (+27.7% YoY) and EBIT margin of 12.2%, up from the prior year. The quant panel shows a business that is fundamentally sound on returns (ROE ~14.8%, ROCE ~19.5%, interest coverage ~7.0x) and has compounded revenue at 16.6% over 3 years with 1-year growth accelerating to 19.8% - both quality and growth scores in the low-to-high 60s confirm this is not a broken business.

The complication is what happens next. Management has guided FY27 revenue growth of only 10-13% in constant currency, with EBIT margin guided to a narrow 12.25-12.75% band - i.e., a deceleration from the 19.7% actually delivered in FY26, and margin expansion that is real but modest (roughly flat to +50bps). Some of FY26's growth and margin recovery has been M&A-assisted (the TeleMedik healthcare-BPO acquisition, alongside the earlier Sourcepoint mortgage-services deal), and debt was raised for these deals before being paid down post-TeleMedik - this is a normal build-by-acquisition BPM strategy, not an accounting red flag, but it does mean some of the reported growth is inorganic rather than pure organic compounding. The stock's price action (down ~23% over 12 months, down ~16% over 6 months, despite the fundamentals above) tells its own story: the market is discounting the entire BPM/call-center services model for GenAI disruption risk - the fear that agentic AI compresses the very transaction-processing and voice-support work Firstsource sells at scale. That fear may be overdone or underdone; either way it is the dominant variable an investor in this name is actually underwriting, more than the reported numbers.

Balance sheet: D/E of ~0.67x is moderate for a services company that has funded bolt-on M&A with debt; interest coverage of ~7x is comfortable, not a stress signal. No governance flags surfaced in this research pass.
recommendation_rationale: The quant composite scores this Hold on both the 3-year (54.3) and 1-year (59.4) windows and I have no analytical basis to override that - fundamentals (mid-teens ROE/ROCE, comfortable coverage, genuine double-digit growth) support a Hold on an existing position, but management's own FY27 guidance (10-13% CC growth, near-flat margins) does not clear the bar for a re-rating case, and the GenAI-disruption overhang on BPM as a category is a real, unresolved risk rather than a reason to argue for anything more constructive than Hold.
summary: Firstsource had a strong FY26 - crossing $1 billion in revenue for the first time with profit growing faster than sales - and the underlying return ratios (mid-teens ROE, high-teens ROCE) are healthy for a business-services company. But management's own guidance for the coming year points to slower growth (10-13%) and only modest margin improvement, some of the recent growth has come from acquisitions rather than pure organic demand, and the stock has fallen sharply over the past year as markets worry about AI eventually automating the call-center and back-office work this company sells. We see this as a fundamentally solid, fairly-valued Hold rather than a name to add to on weakness or to exit outright.
positive_para: A genuine scale milestone ($1B revenue, first time) achieved with profit growing faster than revenue (normalized PAT +26.9% vs revenue +19.7% in FY26); healthy capital efficiency (ROE ~14.8%, ROCE ~19.5%) for a labor-services model; comfortable interest coverage (~7x) even after debt-funded M&A; a diversified vertical mix (healthcare, BFS, CMT) that reduces single-client/single-industry concentration risk; management commentary of a record deal pipeline heading into FY27.
negative_para: FY27 guidance of 10-13% constant-currency growth is a step down from the 19.7% actually delivered in FY26, and part of that FY26 growth was M&A-assisted (TeleMedik, Sourcepoint) rather than pure organic expansion - the market may be right to apply a lower multiple to blended growth. EBIT margin guidance (12.25-12.75%) implies only marginal operating leverage despite the revenue scale-up, and one sell-side note flagged the strong headline quarter as masking underlying margin pressure. Most importantly, the entire BPM/voice-and-transaction-processing category faces a structural question of whether GenAI/agentic automation compresses the addressable market and pricing over the medium term - this is not a one-off but a genuine multi-year sector risk that the -23% 12-month stock return is already partly pricing in, and it is not one we can resolve from the outside.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~28x trailing earnings for a business now guided to 10-13% constant-currency growth and roughly flat margins, the multiple prices in more durable growth than management itself is promising for the next year - i.e., it assumes either sustained M&A-led acceleration back toward high-teens growth, or a market view that BPM providers with strong healthcare/BFS franchises are relative winners (not losers) from AI tooling. Both are plausible but neither is proven yet, so I'd call the stock fair-to-slightly-rich rather than cheap; it does not scream value at current levels, nor is it so extended that a Hold is unjustifiable.
